coaching.title: Easy 5 mi Z2 + Strength
coaching.message: Peak phase, 6 weeks out. Today is a recovery-paced 5 miles, HR strictly 138-150 bpm — if you can't hold a full conversation, slow down. This run is the connective tissue between yesterday's hill descents and your next quality block, so keep it boringly aerobic. Pair it with Strength Session 2: eccentric work (slow tempo split squats, step-downs, Nordic curls) and plyos (pogos, box drops) to armor your quads and tendons for 2,500m of Julian Alps descending. Finish with 10 min of core. Run first light before the El Salvador heat builds.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: It's a short easy run, so no in-run fueling needed — a small carb top-up (banana or a few dates) beforehand is plenty. The real work is post-strength: hit 30-40g protein within the recovery window to drive the eccentric-damage repair you just stimulated, plus carbs to refill. Sit around 220-250g carbs for the day since load is light. In the heat, front-load 600-800mg sodium and stay ahead on fluids even on an easy morning.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Eccentric and plyo work leaves micro-damage that peaks 24-48h later, so today's job is to blunt it: 10 min easy spin or walk to flush the legs, foam-roll quads and calves tonight, and get elastic compression or legs-up-the-wall if the travel day allows. Prioritize sleep — aim 8+ hours. Tomorrow's quality session depends on how well you absorb this one.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Peak phase rewards patience, not heroics. The temptation this close to the Julian Alps is to turn every run into a test — resist it. Discipline on an easy day is what lets you unleash on the hard days. Every controlled descent and clean strength rep now is a deposit against the quad-trashing downhills of Kranjska Gora. Train the humility to go slow; the mountain will ask for everything else.
